acceptance_criteria.criterion: The Ledger Bootstrapper persona source (`personas/ledger-support/src/content/ledger-bootstrapper.md`) includes instructions to craft a `project_summary` from the plan's `## Summary` section.
The instructions specify the summary should be 2–3 sentences, plain text, factual, and describe the project's intent (not implementation details).
The instructions specify passing the summary as the `project_summary` parameter to `ledger_initialize_project`.
Running `node scripts/build-personas.js --check` reports no stale output.

summary: Updated Step 2 of the Ledger Bootstrapper Bootstrapping Protocol to include `project_summary` curation instructions: read the plan's `## Summary` section, craft a 2–3 sentence plain-text factual summary (no markdown, focused on intent not implementation), and pass it as `project_summary` to `ledger_initialize_project`. Added a fallback rule for plans with no `## Summary` section. Rebuilt all 120 persona files successfully; `--check` reports no stale output.

comments.note: The example sentence added to the `project_summary` guidance in `ledger-bootstrapper.md` uses this plan's own content as the sample — a natural, self-documenting choice. Future editors should update the example to reflect a different, more generic project if the wording becomes confusing. File: `personas/ledger-support/src/content/ledger-bootstrapper.md`, Step 2.

The fallback rule ('If the plan has no `## Summary` section: Omit the `project_summary` parameter') is reasonable but could be extended to fall back to the plan's first paragraph. This is out of scope for this WP but worth noting for future refinement.

summary: All 5 ACs pass. Source prose is clear, actionable, and correctly specifies the project_summary constraints. All 3 generated output targets contain the new instructions. Build check passes with 120 personas and no stale output.

Reviewed the `project_summary` curation instructions added to Step 2 of the Ledger Bootstrapper protocol. The prose is clean, well-constrained, and actionable — three explicit quality constraints (factual+concise, plain-text only, intent-focused), a concrete example, and a correct fallback for missing Summary sections. All 3 output targets (vs-code, claude-code, deep-agents) confirmed to contain the new instructions at 4 matches each. Build passes with 120 personas and no stale output. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: The example in Step 2 of `ledger-bootstrapper.md` uses the current plan's own description as sample text — self-referential but functional. If a future reader encounters this out of context, they may not recognise it as an example sentence. Consider replacing with a more generic project description when the content is next edited.

Missing edge case: Step 2 handles the case where `## Summary` is absent (omit parameter), but does not guard against a section that is present but empty or too brief (e.g. a single-word heading). A brief note — 'If the Summary section is too short to yield 2–3 sentences, omit the parameter rather than inventing content' — would close this gap.

No observations beyond the two minor notes above — the source prose is clear, the build system propagates the change correctly to all 3 output targets, and the architectural fit within the bootstrapping protocol is sound.
